metadata.notes: agent=yes, daemon=bug, driver=ready — muse genuinely detaches a slow bash command (tool_batch.effect.terminal.outcome.task_completion.kind=="pending", 1/374 real corpus examples) with runtime-injected guidance confirming it's an intentional feature, but the muse parser observes NONE of the events needed to derive BackgroundProcessCount (task_stream_linked, tool_batch.effect.*, and the task's own kind:"task" lifecycle are all explicitly skipped) — record-known-failing, file an issue.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: bug; driver_capability: ready

Route: record-known-failing. Muse genuinely runs a detached background shell command (its own equivalent of Claude Code's run_in_background); the muse adapter's parser observes NONE of the events that would let it derive BackgroundProcessCount, so the dashboard-visible count required by the scenario's acceptance criteria can never be non-zero today. Record it known_failing (spec asserts the CORRECT behavior) and file an issue — the trace exists, this is a parser gap, not an architecture limit.

## agent_supports: yes

Muse's active toolset (confirmed live, `model_request_configured.toolset.active_tools`) carries both `bash` (launch) and `bash_input` (interact with/poll/kill a running shell) — the direct analog of Claude Code's Bash + BashOutput + KillShell. Every bash call is routed through an internal streaming execution subsystem (`"system":"unified_exec"` / `managed_bash_task_attempt` in the binary's own schema strings) that CAN detach a long-running command and keep it alive past the tool call's own return. When a command exceeds a foreground-wait ceiling, the runtime hands control back to the model with `tool_batch.effect.terminal.record.outcome.task_completion.kind == "pending"` (instead of `"terminal"`) while the process keeps running, and a `status` event on the task carries `details.facets:[{"kind":"live_process","system":"unified_exec"}]`. The tool's own injected output carries explicit runtime guidance confirming this is an intentional, documented feature, not an accident: `"The command is still running in the background and the UI already shows its status. Do not poll for completion: the final output is delivered to you automatically as runtime context and wakes you even after you end the turn. ..."`. On completion the task reaches its own terminal lifecycle event (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`rejected`) and gets queued for delivery via `event.kind:"inbox_item_queued"` (`source.source:"background_task_terminal"`, carrying `terminal_kind`), later drained via `inbox_item_drained`.

This is drawn from real on-disk evidence, not just docs: a corpus-wide scan of every `session.jsonl` under `~/.local/share/muse/sessions` on this machine (191 files, this machine's real usage history including onboarding-factory's own prior live probes) found 374 real `task_kind:"tool.bash"` `tool_batch.effect.terminal` records; exactly 1 had `task_completion.kind:"pending"` (a genuinely detached ~99s `grep -rn "muse" ...` repo search, session `01a09c47-.../subagent/01a09c6d-9715-.../session.jsonl`, task_id `01a09c6f-1b6d-76a0-bb62-ba61192c3616`); the other 373 resolved synchronously (`"terminal"`) within ≤7.66s of their own `started` event. This 1-in-374 ratio confirms the feature is real and intentional, and that it is genuinely rare/hard to trigger by accident — a recipe needs a deliberately slow command.

## daemon_capability: bug (trace exists; the parser is 100% silent on all of it)

Source-read of `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go` on this branch: every event that carries the background-process signal is explicitly, deliberately unhandled:

- The outer `route()` dispatcher's default arm (parser.go:236-242) skips the top-level `tool_batch.effect.started`/`tool_batch.effect.terminal` payload types outright — this is exactly where `outcome.task_completion.kind` (the "pending" vs "terminal" discriminator) lives, so the signal never reaches the daemon in any form.
- `parseRunEvent`'s own default arm (parser.go:290-297) explicitly lists `task_stream_linked` and `inbox_item_queued`/`inbox_item_drained`/`inbox_delivery_anomaly` among the "high-volume internal bookkeeping this stage has no use for" and skips them.
- `kind:"task"` events (`proposed/accepted/started/status/output/completed/...` — the task's own lifecycle, including its terminal outcome) are skipped at `parseSessionEnvelope`'s default arm.

So `session.SessionMetrics.BackgroundProcessCount` is never set for muse today — full stop. This alone is `bug`, not `incapable`: no live liveness probe (lsof) would even be needed the way Claude Code needs one, since muse durably records BOTH "still running" (`task_completion.kind:"pending"`) and the definitive termination (the task's own terminal event / `inbox_item_queued.terminal_kind`) directly in the transcript the daemon already tails — the parser is simply wired to ignore all of it.

**A pre-existing dismissal in this same file needs a precise correction, per this repo's "dismissals carry evidence" convention.** The package doc at parser.go:59-74 already reasons about `tool_batch.effect.*` and concludes duplication: *"tool_batch.effect.terminal's outcome.kind never showed a genuine 'failed' example in this corpus (489 'completed', 1 'cancelled')... pure duplication with no additional signal."* I independently confirmed that same near-uniform distribution on the OUTER `outcome.kind` field. But that field is one level up from `outcome.task_completion.kind` — a DIFFERENT, nested field in the identical record that the doc's own scan did not examine, and which is the actual background-process discriminator. The "pure duplication, no additional signal" conclusion is correct for ordinary tool-call success/failure tracking (which is all the doc claims) but does not extend to this scenario: `task_completion.kind` carries information the simpler `assistant_tool_calls_committed`/`tool_result_batch_committed` pair the parser currently uses has no equivalent for. The fix needs a new, narrow read of this one nested field, not a reuse of anything already wired — and the existing comment should get a follow-up note once that lands, so a future reader does not re-conclude "pure duplication" and skip it again.

**Open question `record` must settle — state-hold vs. dashboard-count-only gap.** Unlike claudecode/gemini-cli/hermes/copilot (whose OWN agent turn genuinely closes while the detached process keeps running, which is exactly why each needs BackgroundProcessCount to prevent settling to `ready` too early), muse's `run.terminal` — which the parser already turns into `EventType:"turn_done"` (parser.go:317-325), the daemon's existing, unmodified working→ready trigger — empirically never fired before its enclosing run's own background bash tasks resolved, in every one of 372 real `execution_mode:"background"` `task_kind:"tool.bash"` spawns found across the local 191-session corpus (0 counter-examples; scanned via sequence-number ordering of each task's own terminal event against its run's own `("run","terminal")` event). That is suggestive that the STATE-HOLD half of the scenario ("stays working") may already be correct today with zero daemon changes — muse's own runtime may hold the run open until backgrounded work resolves, architecturally unlike the four sibling agents. But the corpus never contains a case where the model tried to end its own conversational turn WHILE a background task was still genuinely pending — in the one real "pending" example, the model simply kept issuing unrelated tool calls for ~99 more seconds, so the turn never attempted to close early regardless of the background task. The tool's own injected guidance text ("...wakes you even after you end the turn") is also readable the OPPOSITE way — that the turn CAN genuinely close (a premature `ready`) and a later, separate run/wake redelivers the result, mirroring the two-cycle "parent goes ready, child continues, parent wakes later" shape this same scenario family's sibling `background-subagent` (3.2) explicitly documents for subagent backgrounding. Static evidence cannot resolve this; only `record`'s live recording (recipe below deliberately instructs the model to reply immediately after backgrounding, exactly mirroring the sibling agents' recipes) can, and should correct/confirm this caveat via `observability_correction`.

The `BackgroundProcessCount` gap is unambiguous by itself (a complete, confirmed source read, no live-recording dependency), so `daemon=bug` holds regardless of how the state-hold question resolves — at worst `record` narrows the caveat; it should not flip the pillar to `full`, since the dashboard count would stay 0 either way.

## driver_capability: ready

The recipe needs only `send` + `wait_turn` (+ `sleep` for the settle tail), all implemented in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` (`send|slash`, `wait_turn`, `sleep` case arms, ~line 666-676). No `keys`/`interrupt` gap: muse auto-promotes a long bash call to background execution on its own — the model never has to flip an explicit flag, and its own runtime guidance actively discourages manual `bash_input` polling, so a plain single-prompt `send`+`wait_turn` recipe brackets the whole arc.

## Confidence 0.7

High confidence (agent_supports, and the BackgroundProcessCount parser gap itself) rests on direct, unambiguous evidence — 374 real corpus records for the former, a complete source read for the latter. Held to 0.7 (not higher) by the one genuine open question above (whether the state-hold half already works or shares the sibling agents' premature-ready bug), which only a live recording can settle.
caveats: LOAD-BEARING for any future daemon fix: task_stream_linked.execution_mode=="background" is NOT a usable background-process discriminator on its own — it is present on effectively ALL bash calls (374/374 in the local corpus) regardless of duration, and is ALSO used for subagent spawns (task_kind:"workflow.agent.native", 26 instances) and internal reminder micro-agents (task_kind:"reminder.agent.*", 236 instances) sharing the identical execution_mode:"background" label — the exact background-process-vs-subagent conflation this cell was scoped to avoid. The correct signal is tool_batch.effect.terminal.record.outcome.task_completion.kind=="pending" (vs "terminal") on a task_id whose task_kind (from its own "proposed" event) is "tool.bash", paired with that same task_id's own later terminal task event to clear it.

OPEN QUESTION for record to settle: whether muse's run.terminal genuinely stays gated on a pending background bash task when the MODEL itself tries to end its turn early (untested locally — every corpus example of a pending task coincided with the model doing unrelated work anyway), or whether the turn can close and a later separate run/wake redelivers the result (the background-subagent (3.2) shape). Either way BackgroundProcessCount stays unpopulated today, so daemon=bug holds; record should use observability_correction to narrow this caveat, not to flip the pillar.

Small main-session sample: only 28 tool.bash calls were found in top-level (non-subagent) sessions locally, none genuinely backgrounded (0 pending). The one real pending example came from a subagent session. The tool_batch/task protocol is identical regardless of which session owns the run, so there is no structural reason to expect a difference, but this is not independently confirmed for a main session.

The auto-background threshold is empirically bounded to (7.66s, 10.02s] from a single natural corpus example (max observed synchronous resolution vs. the one genuinely pending case), not from a controlled test. The recipe uses a 20s sleep for a safety margin; record should note the actual observed threshold if the live recording's timing differs materially.

cost_nonzero must stay false: muse-spark-1.3-contributor has no pricing/alias entry (core/pkg/capacity), the same established muse-wide fact used across every other muse cell in this onboarding pass (re-confirmed live on this machine's most recent 2026-09-14 sessions, still muse-spark-1.3-contributor).

Muse spawns companion reminder/goal-check subagents freely during any turn (skill-reminder/goal-reminder/verify-reminder — 111/57/57 instances in the local corpus, ALSO tagged execution_mode:"background"). Every phase is pinned same_session_as:session_birth to rule out the vacuous-pass mechanism this column's sibling cells (2-2, 2-17) already hit from an unpinned phase silently matching a companion subagent's own arc.

sources.note: Lines 59-74: package-doc dismissal of tool_batch.effect.* as "pure duplication" based on the OUTER outcome.kind field only (489 completed/1 cancelled) — does not examine the nested outcome.task_completion.kind field, which is the actual background-process discriminator. Lines 236-242: route()'s default arm skips top-level tool_batch.effect.started/terminal entirely. Lines 290-297: parseRunEvent's default arm explicitly names task_stream_linked and inbox_item_queued/drained/inbox_delivery_anomaly as unhandled. Lines 317-325: parseRunTerminal sets EventType="turn_done" from the run's own terminal event — the daemon's existing, unmodified working→ready trigger.

The one genuine local example of a detached background bash task: sequence 561 task_stream_linked execution_mode:background task_kind:tool.bash (task_id 01a09c6f-...); sequence 567-568 tool_batch.effect.started/terminal, the terminal record's outcome.task_completion.kind:"pending" ~10.03s after task start; sequence 569 status event with details.facets [{kind:live_process,system:unified_exec}]; sequence 570 output event chunk carrying execution_state:"background_running" and the runtime's injected model_guidance text ("...wakes you even after you end the turn... Do not poll..."); sequences 979-984 (~99s later) the task's own completed event plus inbox_item_queued (source.source:background_task_terminal, terminal_kind:completed) and an output chunk with exit_code:0/terminal_status:completed; sequence 1010 inbox_item_drained. The enclosing run's own ("run","terminal") event is the file's LAST line (sequence 1675, ~105s after the background task itself resolved).

sources.note: Produced: task_kind=="tool.bash" cross-tabulated against execution_mode gives 374 background / 0 foreground (i.e. execution_mode:background is universal for bash, not discriminating); task_completion.kind distribution for those same 374 is 373 "terminal" (max 7.659s from started) + 1 "pending" (10.017s); of the 372 genuine background tool.bash spawns whose enclosing run reached its own terminal event, 0 had the background task still unresolved when the run went terminal (372/372 resolved first, 348 from subagent sessions + 28 from... wait see caveats for the main/subagent split note).
Lines ~666-676: send|slash, wait_turn, sleep case arms implemented; keys/interrupt/reset_session/resume remain not_implemented (irrelevant to this recipe, which needs none of them).
Confirms bash + bash_input are both in the default active toolset (alongside subagent_spawn/wait/read_result etc.), matching the scenario's Bash+BashOutput analog.

preconditions: irrlichd is recording (isolated dev daemon with --record). NOTE: this cell is known_failing — the current muse adapter cannot derive BackgroundProcessCount, so the recording is expected to fail the bg_alive_working phase's duration hold OR (if record's live probe confirms the optimistic state-hold hypothesis in the assessment body) may pass that phase while the dashboard count itself remains unverifiable by this spec format — either way, use observability_correction to record what actually happened.
muse launched with --trust-workspace (skip the first-run workspace-trust dialog) in a throwaway cwd; default :auto-review approval profile is fine — a plain `sleep` command needs no approval.
setup: Driver launches muse in a fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd; no seed files needed — the background process is a self-contained sleep && echo.

script.text: Do exactly this and nothing else, in a single turn. Use the bash tool to run the command `sleep 20 && echo BG_DONE`. As soon as that tool call returns control to you — whether or not the command has actually finished — reply immediately with exactly the word: BGPROC_OK. Do NOT poll or check on the command again, do NOT run any other commands, and do NOT narrate that it started or is running — just run it once and reply with the literal token.

verify: session.jsonl contains a task with task_kind:"tool.bash" whose tool_batch.effect.terminal record has outcome.task_completion.kind=="pending" (the genuine-detach signal, not merely task_stream_linked.execution_mode=="background", which is present on essentially every bash call)

session.jsonl contains that same task_id's own later terminal task event (kind:"completed") and the matching inbox_item_queued (source.source:"background_task_terminal", terminal_kind:"completed") plus inbox_item_drained

KNOWN FAILING (BackgroundProcessCount half): events.jsonl is EXPECTED to show BackgroundProcessCount/HasLiveBackgroundProcess-equivalent tracking absent throughout — the muse parser sets neither, so this metric-level half of the acceptance criteria cannot be observed by this spec format regardless of the recording's outcome.

OPEN (state-hold half): whether the bg_alive_working phase below passes or fails is the open empirical question the assessment body names — record whichever it is and set observability_correction accordingly (do not silently reconcile a pass into the known_failing note without updating it).
primary session is born ready and binds a PID within ~2s of launch
